content.comment_body: Hello, Is it possible to expand a [product_name] [article_no] with a 230V AC power supply by adding a [product_name] [article_no] digital expansion module designed for 24V? I understand each module needs a different power supply, but will they be able to communicate together safely without causing any damage? Thanks for your response.

You cannot directly connect a 24VDC digital expansion module to a 230VAC base module or a 230VAC digital expansion module. The internal bus for communication is not electrically isolated. An analog expansion module must be inserted between them because it provides the required electrical isolation. For example: 230VAC base module -> 230VAC digital module -> analog expansion module -> 24VDC digital module
So, the analog expansion module provides bus isolation, while the digital expansion modules do not. Thanks for the clarification. That was very informative!

analysis.insight_summary: Users addressed the compatibility and safety concerns of connecting digital expansion modules with differing voltages to a base module. The discussion clarified that only analog expansion modules provide electrical isolation on the bus, making them necessary to interpose between modules operating at different voltages to avoid potential damage and ensure proper communication.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to safely expand a 230VAC base module by adding 24VDC digital expansion modules, aiming for reliable communication and no risk of equipment damage.
